summary: A running timeline from Sporting News of the Michigan sign-stealing scandal, centered on staffer Connor Stalions, from Nov. 3 to Nov. 17, 2023. The Big Ten suspended coach Jim Harbaugh for three games for violating its sportsmanship policy, Michigan fought the suspension in court and then dropped its suit and accepted it. The NCAA probe continues, with linebackers coach Chris Partridge fired over alleged evidence destruction.
one_line: Timeline of Michigan's sign-stealing scandal, Jim Harbaugh's three-game Big Ten suspension, legal fight, and the firing of coach Chris Partridge in November 2023.
key_facts: The Big Ten suspended Jim Harbaugh for the remaining three regular-season games, including the Ohio State rivalry game, on Nov. 10, 2023, finding Michigan violated the Big Ten Sportsmanship Policy through an 'impermissible, in-person scouting operation over multiple years.'
The Big Ten could not prove Harbaugh knew of the scheme; it said that as head coach he 'embodies the university for purposes of its football program' and is responsible for preventing such schemes.

Michigan filed a temporary restraining order in Washtenaw County Trial Court on Nov. 10; no ruling came before the Penn State game, so Harbaugh did not coach and Sherrone Moore served as acting head coach.

On Nov. 16, Michigan and Harbaugh dropped litigation against the Big Ten and accepted the three-game suspension; the Big Ten closed its investigation and said it knew of no information suggesting Harbaugh's involvement.
On Nov. 17, Yahoo Sports reported that Connor Stalions was at least partially funded by a Michigan booster named 'Uncle T.'
Linebackers coach Chris Partridge was fired by Michigan on Nov. 17 and is alleged to have destroyed evidence on a computer; he is not believed to have had prior knowledge of the scheme.
Connor Stalions resigned from Michigan on Nov. 3, 2023; he is accused of buying numerous tickets to scout future opponents in person, which NCAA rules have prohibited for nearly 30 years.
Michigan's 10-page letter to the Big Ten argued a punishment before a full NCAA investigation was premature and said in-person scouting and sign-stealing may be 'far more prevalent than believed.'

Michigan shared evidence that staff at Ohio State, Purdue and Rutgers shared decoded Michigan signals before the 2022 Big Ten Championship Game, as reported by The Athletic; Ohio State coach Ryan Day denied it.
Athletic director Warde Manuel called the suspension 'completely unethical' and 'an assault on the rights of everyone (especially in the Big Ten) to be judged by a fair and complete investigation.'
Harbaugh had already served a self-imposed three-game suspension at the start of the season in a separate NCAA investigation that found he lied to investigators.
Biff Poggi, Charlotte's first-year head coach, invited Harbaugh to join the 49ers' sideline for games vs. Rice and at South Florida on Nov. 25.
